req_desc: The site reads as one continuous surface rather than as a set of separate pages ...
Every seeded account signs in with the pinned password `deku-demo-pw-2026` ...
A signup always produces a reader role, whatever the request body asks for.
An unauthenticated studio route is denied, redirecting the page to sign in ...
A signup with an existing email is refused, writing no second account row.
An expired token is denied on every protected route.
A password hash is never returned by any endpoint.
The project list returns published projects in order.
A project area renders with a thousands separator: `58,079 m2`.
A project detail carries its body beside its gallery image rows.
Team, offices, awards, publications are all ordered collections of the content model.
The legal route carries eight numbered chapters.
Gallery photographs feed the arc in order from the content model.
The arc settings record is one editable record holding every arc parameter.
An editor creates a project from the studio surface with no code change.
An image reference carries alt text, a ratio, a seed rather than a file path.
A draft project is absent from every public list ...
A draft object is not publicly readable from the bucket ...
Cover bytes are uploaded to the bucket at the key scheme `projects/{project_id}/{sha256_of_bytes}.png`.
Regenerating an image from one seed writes no second object.
Publishing flips the flag, recording when the flip happened ...
An enquiry is stored with a unique reference of twelve lowercase characters ...
A duplicate enquiry submission creates one row, returning the first reference.
Page views are recorded with their route, readable by an editor alone.
An editor reads every enquiry received, newest first.
A public list query cannot ask for unpublished rows by any parameter.
An invalid enquiry is refused inline, naming the field at fault.
A filled decoy field marks an enquiry invalid, with nothing written ...
An unknown address answers not found under an honest title.
Every internal link on a public route resolves.
The legal route is linked from the signup form as the terms page.
The project index opens in `List` mode.
A chosen view mode survives a move to another route, then back ...
The navigation marks the active route, re-marking on every route change.
A reduced motion request resolves every reveal to its end state ...
Legal chapters expand from the keyboard, exposing whether each is open.
Each heading past the founding block arrives a line at a time on being scrolled into view.
The radial figure behind the statement fades in as the statement is reached.
The fanned photographs rotate, then settle, over the black arc section under scroll.
The three statistics read over black, each a numeral beside a serif label, before the office list closes the route.
The eighth legal chapter carries an illustrative-content statement.
The not-found page carries a link back to the home page beside a line in the studio's voice.
A reveal scrolled half way into its block reads half done ...
The navigation stays legible on crossing from the white hero into the black section.
Every footer entry that is a link opens a real page ...
The contact route reads three contact groups set large in the serif.
The award statements close the about route.
The picture layer meets the layout above with no visible seam.
An empty enquiry list renders its own empty state ...
Pressing `Visit` on a project opens that building's own route.
A sent enquiry lands on a confirmation address showing its reference.
The studio content index opens for a signed-in editor ...
A reduced-motion request leaves the site usable rather than stripped ...
Public routes declare unique titles, each beside its own description, no two sharing either ...
An image row digest matches the stored object bytes ...
Enquiry rows persist, surviving a reread.
Seeding is idempotent across a restart for accounts, projects, images, collections alike.
Project images are unique on the project with the kind, then the order.
Seeding across a restart fills twelve tables whose timestamps are all UTC ...
An existing account email is unique, so a second signup writes no row.
A project slug is unique across the projects table.
No address outside the application is referenced anywhere in the build ...
The health endpoint returns ok once the app is ready behind its production server ...
List endpoints return top level arrays ...
core asks covered by this grader
